paper.title_en: Efficient classical simulation of Fermi-Hubbard models with Kramers symmetry
paper.abstract_en: Quantum Monte Carlo methods are widely used to solve quantum many-body problems. However, rigorous guarantees for their performance are poorly understood, especially for simulating interacting fermions. In this work, we develop a quantum Monte Carlo algorithm for a broad family of fermionic systems exhibiting Kramers time-reversal symmetry, and prove that their partition functions can be estimated in polynomial time. This family, which contains many important classes of Hubbard-type models, is known to both avoid the sign problem and obey a Lee-Yang zero-freeness theorem. Thus our results suggest that these two properties together may enable efficient classical algorithms for quantum many-body systems more broadly.
